evidence: Cic. Att. 13.52.1: inde ambulāvit in lītore
Sen. Ep. 51.4: ēbriōs per lītora errantēs
terms.comment: Where Latin walks by the sea, it walks in lītore: Caesar did so at Puteoli after his siesta, and Seneca’s seaside resort had its crowds per lītora. For a river, rīpa.

terms.gloss: the quays, a town’s built waterfront
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.5.97: ad omnīs crepīdinēs urbis
terms.comment: The stone edges of a harbour town, where ships come in.

phrases.english: After supper we’ll walk along the seafront.
then he took a walk along the shore

phrases.latin: pirāticus myoparō … ūsque ad forum Syrācūsānōrum et ad omnīs crepīdinēs urbis accessit
phrases.english: a pirate skiff came right up to the forum of Syracuse and to every quay of the city

sources: Lewis & Short: litus · Lewis & Short: crepido
